2609.06080.title: PhenoBench: Mapping What a Deeply Phenotyped Human Cohort Can Tell Us
2609.06080.paper_summary: Deeply phenotyped cohorts combine clinical, imaging, molecular, and wearable observations across timescales from seconds to years. This breadth can reveal which measurements inform which health-related questions, but heterogeneous analyses are not directly comparable. We present PhenoBench, an executable benchmark built around the Human Phenotype Project, in which more than 13,000 participants have completed the initial visit. Each question fixes the target, eligible population, timing, and allowed information; its evaluation contract specifies the split, metric, baseline, and claim boundary. The benchmark defines 90 clinically grounded tasks across 15 domains and 26 input modalities. Measurements showed question- and representation-dependent predictive value, including positive, near-zero, and negative changes in held-out performance relative to matched baselines. We used PhenoBench to evaluate emerging tabular foundation models across 160 matched regression comparisons spanning 52 tasks. These models ranked above standard task-specific models in aggregate but, averaged across the three pretrained models within each cell, improved on ridge by a median of only 0.004 $R^2$ (95% CI, 0.002--0.006). We then used the same cohort data and evaluation contracts to evaluate 14 language models, collectively covering 40 tasks spanning phenotype recovery, classification, follow-up forecasting, and participant ordering. Without cohort-specific fitting, language models made informative predictions on some tasks, but showed task-specific capability gaps, shared failures of scale, and rarely surpassed models fitted on the same fields. PhenoBench turns a multimodal longitudinal cohort into a versioned, auditable evaluation system where new questions, measurements, and models can be added without redefining existing comparisons.
2609.06080.paper_summary_zh: 深度表型化的隊列結合了臨床、影像學、分子和可穿戴觀察，時間範圍從秒到年。這種廣度可以揭示哪些測量能夠回答哪些健康相關問題，但異質分析並不直接可比。我們提出了 PhenoBench，一個基於人類表型計畫的可執行基準，其中超過 13,000 名參與者已完成初始訪問。每個問題都固定了目標、合格人群、時間和允許的信息；其評估合約指定了分割、指標、基準和聲明邊界。該基準定義了 15 個領域和 26 種輸入模式下的 90 個臨床基礎任務。測量顯示出問題和表徵依賴的預測價值，包括相對於匹配基準的正變化、接近零的變化和負變化。我們使用 PhenoBench 評估了 160 個匹配回歸比較中的新興表格基礎模型，涵蓋了 52 個任務。這些模型在總體上排名高於標準的任務特定模型，但在每個單元內的三個預訓練模型的平均值上，對於 ridge 的改進中位數僅為 0.004 $R^2$（95% CI，0.002--0.006）。然後，我們使用相同的隊列數據和評估合約來評估 14 個語言模型，這些模型共同涵蓋了 40 個任務，涉及表型恢復、分類、後續預測和參與者排序。在沒有特定於隊列的擬合的情況下，語言模型在某些任務上做出了有意義的預測，但顯示出任務特定的能力差距、共同的規模失敗，並且很少超過在相同領域擬合的模型。PhenoBench 將多模態的縱向隊列轉變為一個版本化的、可審計的評估系統，新的問題、測量和模型可以在不重新定義現有比較的情況下添加進來。
